messages.subject: About setar.sim
parts:
Good day all,
I am trying to do a simulation for a two-threshold SETAR model. Specifically I set the AR parameters as arL=0.85, arM= 1 and arH=0.7, so that the mean reversion is faster in the High regime compared witht the Low regime, and the process follows a random walk in the Middle regime.
    ###
    TvarMat <- c(-1,0.85,1,1,2,0.7) #parameters
    set.seed(123)
    a=setar.sim(n=100,B=TvarMat, type="simul", lag=1,
            nthresh=2,Thresh=c(1,1.5),starting=c(1.25))
    plot(a$serie,type='l') # the timeseries plot
    ###
But when I try to fit the SETAR to the newly simulated data:
    ###
    selectSETAR(a$serie, type='level',m=1, thDelay=0,
                 criterion="SSR",same.lags=TRUE, nthresh=2,plot=FALSE)
    ###
It shows vastly different threshold estimates from the theoretical value of 1 and 1.5: i.e. th1 = 5.63 and th2 = 7.62. I then tried to put these values back into the Thresh argument and redo the simulation, but the results again are not satisfying. Obviously the choice of starting values is important.
My question is: how to specify the correct starting value? Here I choose the threshold to be close to each other ( 1 and 1.5) so that the starting value can be set at 1.25 (the mid point). It's not a problem in the manual file's example (see ?selectSETAR) since in that case it is only a one-threshold model.

Any suggestion is appreciated.

Thanks,
Long

messages.subject: Re: [tsDyn] About setar.sim
parts:
Hi Long

Well I think the graph you made explains everything: the process very quickly jumps in one regime and never comes back into the others. So obviously, the threshold estimates will be very bad.

Remember that in an AR(1) process, the mean is inter/(1-slope). With the values you gave, the inner regimes have mean of 2/(1-0.7)=6.66, and -6.66 for the other one. (see simulation below which finds similar values). Further you are setting a random-walk with drift in the inner process. So I believe this is the most important parameter to play with is the intercepts and slopes of each regime. IN fact, I played with a few values (simu 2 below), and it's tricky to find satisfying values for which the process stays enough in each regime, and hence gives you enough observations for estimation.

Good luck

## Simu 1: check mean is close to 6.66, or -6.66
checkMean <- function(){
  a=setar.sim(n=500,B=TvarMat, type="simul", lag=1,
              nthresh=2,Thresh=c(1,1.5),starting=c(1.25))
  mean(a$serie)
}

MC <- replicate(500, checkMean())

mean(MC[MC>0])
mean(MC[MC<0])


## simu 2: good values? Not really, less observations in low regime...

TvarMat <- c(0.12,0.85, 0.1,1,0.5,0.7) #parameters
# set.seed(123)
a=setar.sim(n=500,B=TvarMat, type="simul", lag=1,
            nthresh=2,Thresh=c(1,1.5),starting=c(1.25),
            rand.gen=function(n) rnorm(n, sd = 0.2))
a$B

But when I try to fit the SETAR to the newly simulated data:
  ###
  selectSETAR(a$serie, type='level',m=1, thDelay=0,
              criterion="SSR",same.lags=TRUE, nthresh=2,plot=FALSE)
